artifacts.summary: Maps the /sapience command onto the already-built sapience-vault-read.sh/sapience-publish.sh/sapience-api-lib.sh interfaces, recommends a fully direct-execution skill (no Agent dispatch, matching skill-literature rather than skill-roadmap/skill-meta), confirms the 4 candidate write surfaces fit under AskUserQuestion's 4-option ceiling, grounds a 'most relevant doc' heuristic in brain_server.py's docs_activity() field, and flags that README.md (not just EXTENSION.md) must be updated to pass check-extension-docs.sh's README/manifest parity gate.

memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh's check_readme_vs_manifest() requires every command name in an extension's manifest.json provides.commands array to appear textually as /<name> in that extension's own README.md -- a separate check from the EXTENSION.md/CLAUDE.md merge target. A dispatch or plan that lists EXTENSION.md as the doc to update for a new command but omits README.md will pass review but fail this deploy gate if README.md still asserts the extension has no command surface.

AskUserQuestion is measured categorically withheld from every Agent-tool dispatch of a named subagent_type, independent of frontmatter (agent-frontmatter-standard.md). skill-roadmap and skill-meta work around this by collecting every user choice in the skill's own execution before dispatching a subagent. A stronger resolution, when the delegated work is not itself judgment-heavy, is to skip the Agent dispatch entirely and do the whole command as a fully direct-execution skill (skill-literature's shape: Bash/Read/Write/Edit/AskUserQuestion, no Agent in allowed-tools) -- this sidesteps the withholding hazard rather than working around it.

Sapience's GET /v1/docs response carries a per-doc activity field ({kind, by, at, text, n?}, confirmed in brain_server.py's docs_activity()) naming the newest head-save/comment/answer/read-mark on that doc plus who did it. This gives a mechanical, code-grounded way to find 'the doc the collaborator most recently touched' (max activity.at where activity.by != me) instead of a vaguer content-similarity heuristic, for any future draft-assembly or reply-targeting feature against this vault.
